title: Swing born in black bands; talent in all colors
summary: Leeman says black bands like Henderson's and Hopkins's were swinging before Goodman, that he felt accepted as an equal, and that great and mediocre musicians come in all colors.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: To me, in the first place, Louis Armstrong was the great forefather -- he was to me, and the great swinging big bands of the era were black -- Fletcher Henderson, for instance, and Kenny's Cottonpickers, Claude Hopkins in the early thirties, large band - they all were to me, great swing groups before publicity and Benny Goodman capitalized on the term 'swing'.

And of course, Ellington was in there, too. The black and white bands swung, and the name 'swing' became the standard accepted logo, and the great soloists in those groups -- my love and inspiration musically, and my getting to play with a great many of those greats later on when I progressed with talent, as a drummer. And I was to be accepted by them. An impossible dream come true for me, during the forties and fifties, that is why I lean toward blacks in my playing -- some or many of my super musical heroes were
black, and I felt I was always accepted by them as an equal -- not just a pretty good white drummer.

And oh yes, by the same token, I've worked with some black musicians with big reputations, who didn't have time and music in his bones, a statement I make with tongue in cheek -- some didn't swing worth a bleep, and played unmercifully out of tune and with bad taste, and on the other hand, some of the great white musicians I played with could never be surpassed for greatness -- black, blue, green or otherwise. Jack Teagarden, Lou McGarity, Billy Butterfield, Venus Huckie, Joe Vanuti, Dave McKenner, Bob Haggard on base, Bobbie Hackett on trumpet, Hank Lawson on trumpet. I'm going to stop here -- I mean, there were so many. Color has no priority to great musicians. Nor to their talent. And God only knows that I've worked with hoards of whites with good reputations of being great swingers, and I will take the liberty of being a little cruel here. There were many who were really freeloading with the union cards, black and white.
I'll sum up by saying it about evens out. To me, God passed out the talent in this world in a dimly lit room.
